//: What `next build` type-checks: the application, not the tests.
The desktop export (npm run build:static) moves src/app/api aside — the
Rust backend replaces those routes — and next build then type-checked
tests/ anyway, where the route handlers are imported directly. Every
route test failed to resolve its module and the export died, so
`npm run build:desktop` could not build the app at all from a clean
checkout. It also meant one broken scratch test blocked a production
Tests are still fully type-checked: `npm run typecheck` uses
.next/dev/types is excluded for the same reason: it is generated by
next dev and names whatever routes existed then, so a stale copy failed
